The phases displayed in these matrices are exact; they are not identified modulo a scalar when the matrices are later placed under a control.

For real $\theta$ and a real unit vector $\mathbf n=(n_x,n_y,n_z)$, define the axis rotation
$$R_{\mathbf n}(\theta):=\exp\!\left(-\frac{i\theta}{2}\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}\right),\qquad R_z(\theta):=R_{(0,0,1)}(\theta).$$
Here $\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ and $\|\mathbf n\|_2$ have the meanings fixed in [[def-qc-bloch-coordinate-map]]. For a bounded endomorphism $B$ of $Q_2$, the notation $\exp(B)$ means the operator-norm series $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}B^k/k!$ of [[lem-exponential-series-of-a-bounded-operator]] at scalar parameter $1$. Its convergence applies here because $Q_2$ is finite-dimensional and complete and every linear endomorphism of $Q_2$ is bounded ([[cor-finite-dimensional-normed-spaces-are-banach]], [[cor-linear-maps-with-finite-dimensional-domain-are-bounded]]).

For $\alpha\in\mathbb R$, let
$P_\alpha=\operatorname{diag}(1,e^{i\alpha})$ and
$J(\alpha)=H P_\alpha$, with $H$ and the exact one-qubit gate convention
from [[def-qc-one-qubit-gate-alphabet-and-rotations]]. Define the ordered
measurement vectors

$$ |b\rangle_\alpha:=J(\alpha)^\dagger|b\rangle,\qquad b\in\{0,1\}, $$

where $|0\rangle,|1\rangle$ are the ordered computational basis vectors.
The adjoint and complex inner product use the root convention translated by
[[def-qc-dirac-notation-conversion]]. The global phase in $J(\alpha)$

derivations.claim: Since $|e^{i\alpha}|=1$, $P_\alpha^\dagger P_\alpha=I$. Direct multiplication from [F1] gives $H^\dagger=H$ and $H^2=I$, so [F2] gives $J(\alpha)^\dagger J(\alpha)=P_\alpha^\dagger H^\dagger H P_\alpha=I$. Hence $J(\alpha)^\dagger$ maps the orthonormal computational basis to an orthonormal basis.

Substituting $\alpha=0$ in [F2] gives $J(0)=H$, and therefore $J(0)^2=H^2=I$. Matrix multiplication using [F1] and [F2] gives $J(-\beta)X=\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}e^{-i\beta}&1\\-e^{-i\beta}&1\end{pmatrix}$ and $e^{-i\beta}ZJ(\beta)=\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}e^{-i\beta}&1\\-e^{-i\beta}&1\end{pmatrix}$, proving the exact phase identity.

From [F1] and [F2], $J(\pi/2)=\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&i\\1&-i\end{pmatrix}$. Multiplying this matrix three times gives $J(\pi/2)^3=\frac{1+i}{\sqrt2}I=e^{i\pi/4}I$. This phase will be retained in the transport normalization.

For a real angle $\theta$, define the one-qubit phase matrix $P_\theta=\operatorname{diag}(1,e^{i\theta})$. In control-first order define

$$CP(\theta):=C(P_\theta)=\operatorname{diag}(1,1,1,e^{i\theta})$$

in the ordered basis $|00\rangle,|01\rangle,|10\rangle,|11\rangle$. This is the exact controlled phase; no circuit cost or controlled access to an arbitrary black-box unitary is implied.

Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph with a fixed order
$V=(v_0,\ldots,v_{n-1})$. Put $\mathbb F_2:=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$; the
field law follows from [[thm-z-mod-p-is-a-field]] at $p=2$, and this field has
order two by [[def-finite-field-and-its-order]]. Define the binary adjacency
matrix $A_2(G)\in M_n(\mathbb F_2)$ by

$$ (A_2(G))_{jk}=\begin{cases}1,&\{v_j,v_k\}\in E,\\0,&\{v_j,v_k\}\notin E.\end{cases} $$

The indices use the ordered bit coordinates of
[[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]]. Since edges are unordered pairs of
distinct vertices, $A_2(G)$ is symmetric and has zero diagonal. This is a
matrix over $\mathbb F_2$, using [[def-matrices-over-a-commutative-ring]];
it is not the root library's real-valued adjacency matrix. When $V=\varnothing$,
$A_2(G)$ is the unique $0\times0$ matrix.

The displayed tensor powers are tensor maps on the ordered factors, using [[def-qc-tensor-map]].
Fix an integer $n\ge 1$. Let $\mathcal H_n=Q_2^{\otimes n}$ be the ordered tensor register of $n$ qubits from [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], and let $\mathbb F_2=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$. We name the wires $1,\ldots,n$; wire $j$ is position $j-1$ in the source's $0$-based factor list. Bit tuples use the big-endian encoding from [[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]], so the first wire is the most significant bit. Write $X_j$ and $Z_j$ for the tensor maps with the displayed one-qubit matrix on wire $j$ and the identity on every other wire. For $x,z\in\mathbb F_2^n$, set $X^x=\bigotimes_{j=1}^n X^{x_j}$ and $Z^z=\bigotimes_{j=1}^n Z^{z_j}$, where an exponent $0$ means the identity on that factor and an exponent $1$ means the displayed Pauli matrix. For $k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z$, define

$$P(k,x,z):=i^kX^xZ^z.$$

The **phase-aware $n$-qubit Pauli set** $\mathcal P_n$ is the set of these operators with matrix multiplication. Its scalar subset is $Z_n:=\{i^k I_{\mathcal H_n}:k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z\}$. The product-and-adjoint theorem proves that $\mathcal P_n$ is a group and that $Z_n$ is its center.

An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

derivations.claim: For $y\in\mathbb F_2^n$, write $q_M(y)=\sum_{\{j,k\}\in M}y_jy_k$. By [F1], $CZ_M|y\rangle=(-1)^{q_M(y)}|y\rangle$. Expanding each edge term over $\mathbb F_2$ gives the cross term $\sum_{\{j,k\}\in M}(y_jx_k+x_jy_k)$. By the stated coordinate order and dot-product convention, $(A_Mx)_j=\sum_{k:\{j,k\}\in M}x_k$, so this cross term is exactly $(A_Mx)\cdot y$. Hence $q_M(y\oplus x)=q_M(y)+q_M(x)+(A_Mx)\cdot y$.

Applying the left side of the claimed identity to $|y\rangle$ gives $(-1)^{z\cdot y+q_M(y\oplus x)}|y\oplus x\rangle$. Applying the right side gives $(-1)^{q_M(x)+q_M(y)+(z\oplus A_Mx)\cdot y}|y\oplus x\rangle$; step 1.1 makes these signs equal. The ordered computational basis spans the register, so the operators agree. When $n=0$ or $M=\varnothing$, every sum is empty and both sides are the identity frame relation by [F3]--[F4].

For $\alpha\in\mathbb R$, let
$P_\alpha=\operatorname{diag}(1,e^{i\alpha})$ and
$J(\alpha)=H P_\alpha$, with $H$ and the exact one-qubit gate convention
from [[def-qc-one-qubit-gate-alphabet-and-rotations]]. Define the ordered
measurement vectors

$$ |b\rangle_\alpha:=J(\alpha)^\dagger|b\rangle,\qquad b\in\{0,1\}, $$

where $|0\rangle,|1\rangle$ are the ordered computational basis vectors.
The adjoint and complex inner product use the root convention translated by
[[def-qc-dirac-notation-conversion]]. The global phase in $J(\alpha)$
is fixed by the displayed matrix product; it is not suppressed.

For every $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb R$, $J(\alpha)$ is unitary and
$\{|0\rangle_\alpha,|1\rangle_\alpha\}$ is an orthonormal basis. The exact
identities

$$ J(0)=H,\qquad J(0)^2=I,\qquad J(-\beta)X=e^{-i\beta}ZJ(\beta),\qquad J(\pi/2)^3=e^{i\pi/4}I $$

hold in the fixed phase convention.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty outcome set ([[def-dimension]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). Its **endomorphisms** are its complex-linear maps $H\to H$ ([[def-vector-space-of-linear-maps]]); for an endomorphism $P$, $P^*$ denotes its adjoint, which exists uniquely in finite dimension ([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]], [[thm-adjoint-exists-and-is-unique-in-finite-dimension]]). A **finite projective measurement** on $H$ with outcomes $\Omega$ is a family $(P_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ of endomorphisms such that

$$P_a^*=P_a,\qquad P_a^2=P_a,\qquad P_aP_b=0\ (a\ne b),\qquad \sum_{a\in\Omega}P_a=I_H.$$

The products above are compositions, the sum is pointwise addition of endomorphisms, and $I_H$ is the identity map; these operations preserve linear maps ([[prop-linear-maps-form-a-vector-space]], [[lem-composition-and-identity-linear-maps]]). The projections $P_a=0$ are permitted. For a density operator $\rho$ on $H$ (nonnegative and trace one, [[def-qc-density-operator]]), the associated outcome weights are $p_\rho(a)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_a)$; their nonnegativity and normalization are proved in [[thm-qc-projective-measurement-outcome-law]].

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space. Two nonzero vectors $x,y\in H$ represent the same **ray** when $y=\alpha x$ for some nonzero $\alpha\in\mathbb C$. A **pure state** is such a ray. If $u$ is a unit representative, its associated operator is $P_u=|u\rangle\langle u|$, with the bra, ket and outer-product convention of [[def-qc-dirac-notation-conversion]]. The theorem [[thm-qc-ray-projector-well-defined-and-bijective]] proves that this operator is a rank-one orthogonal projection independent of the chosen unit representative, so it is the operator representative of the pure state.

For nonzero finite-dimensional complex-inner-product $H$, the map sending a ray $[u]$ to the rank-one projector $P_u=|u\rangle\langle u|$ of any unit representative is well-defined and bijective onto the rank-one orthogonal projections on $H$. Each $P_u$ is non-negative and has trace one.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root library's convention that the inner product is linear in its first argument. A **density operator** on $H$ is a non-negative endomorphism $\rho:H\to H$ with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho)=1$; non-negative and trace have the meanings of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]] and [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. The zero-dimensional space is excluded: its only endomorphism has trace $0$.

Here $\ker\rho=\{x\in H:\rho x=0\}$, using the kernel of a linear map from [[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]. The **support** of $\rho$ is the orthogonal complement of its kernel in the root convention:

$$\operatorname{supp}(\rho):=\{x\in H: \langle x,y\rangle=0\text{ for every }y\in\ker\rho\}.$$

For a subspace $S\subseteq H$, $\rho$ is **faithful on $S$** when $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)=S$ and the restriction $\rho|_S:S\to S$ is positive definite in the sense of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]. This restriction is an endomorphism: if $x\in S$ and $y\in\ker\rho$, self-adjointness gives $\langle\rho x,y\rangle=\langle x,\rho y\rangle=0$, so $\rho x\in(\ker\rho)^\perp=S$.

All complex inner products in this track use the root convention: they are
linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second
([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). For vectors $x,y$ in the same
space, define the Dirac pairing by

$$\langle x|y\rangle_D:=\langle y,x\rangle_{\mathrm{root}}.$$

The ket $|x\rangle$ denotes the vector $x$. The bra $\langle x|$ denotes the
linear functional $z\mapsto\langle z,x\rangle_{\mathrm{root}}$.

For finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H,K$, vectors $y\in H$ and
$x\in K$, define the rank-one linear map

$$|x\rangle\langle y|:H\to K,\qquad z\mapsto\langle z,y\rangle_{H,\mathrm{root}}x.$$

Given ordered orthonormal bases of $H$ and $K$, its coordinate matrix is
$[x][y]^\dagger$, where $[x]$ and $[y]$ are the corresponding coordinate
columns and $M^\dagger:=\overline M^{\mathsf T}$ is the conjugate transpose.
The coordinate assertion is established in
[[thm-qc-dirac-notation-coordinate-identity]].

Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces with ordered
orthonormal bases $E=(e_j)_{j<n}$ and $F=(f_i)_{i<m}$. Let $T:H\to K$ be
linear ([[def-linear-map]]), and write $T_{ij}$ for the $(i,j)$ entry of its
matrix in these bases.
Then, for every $z\in H$,

$$Tz=\sum_{j<n}\sum_{i<m}T_{ij}\langle z,e_j\rangle_{H,\mathrm{root}}f_i, \qquad T=\sum_{j<n}\sum_{i<m}T_{ij}|f_i\rangle\langle e_j|.$$

For $x\in K$ and $y\in H$, the rank-one map $|x\rangle\langle y|$ has
coordinate matrix $[x]_F[y]_E^\dagger$, where $M^\dagger=\overline M^{\mathsf T}$.
Its amplitude satisfies
$\langle x|T|y\rangle_D=\langle Ty,x\rangle_{K,\mathrm{root}}$.
All sums are empty when an index dimension is zero, and the identities include
those cases.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $F$ and let $T:V\to V$ be
linear. Choose any ordered basis $\mathcal B$ of $V$ and define the **trace of
the endomorphism $T$** by

$$\operatorname{tr}(T):=\operatorname{tr}([T]_{\mathcal B}^{\mathcal B}).$$

This is independent of the chosen basis: matrices of the same endomorphism in
two ordered bases are similar, and similar matrices have equal trace. When
$V$ is the zero space, the empty basis gives trace $0$.

For $A\in M_{m\times n}(F)$ and $B\in M_{n\times m}(F)$,

$$\operatorname{tr}(AB)=\operatorname{tr}(BA).$$

The two products may have different sizes, and the equality includes $m=0$ or
$n=0$.

Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces with ordered
orthonormal bases $E=(e_j)_{j<n}$ and $F=(f_i)_{i<m}$. Let $T:H\to K$ be
linear ([[def-linear-map]]), and write $T_{ij}$ for the $(i,j)$ entry of its
matrix in these bases.
Then, for every $z\in H$,

$$Tz=\sum_{j<n}\sum_{i<m}T_{ij}\langle z,e_j\rangle_{H,\mathrm{root}}f_i, \qquad T=\sum_{j<n}\sum_{i<m}T_{ij}|f_i\rangle\langle e_j|.$$

For $x\in K$ and $y\in H$, the rank-one map $|x\rangle\langle y|$ has
coordinate matrix $[x]_F[y]_E^\dagger$, where $M^\dagger=\overline M^{\mathsf T}$.
Its amplitude satisfies
$\langle x|T|y\rangle_D=\langle Ty,x\rangle_{K,\mathrm{root}}$.
All sums are empty when an index dimension is zero, and the identities include
those cases.

For $x,y\in\mathbb R^n$ and $z,w\in\mathbb C^n$, the formulas

$$\langle x,y\rangle_{\mathbb R^n}=\sum_{k<n}x_ky_k,\qquad \langle z,w\rangle_{\mathbb C^n}=\sum_{k<n}z_k\overline{w_k}$$

define inner products, linear in the first argument. At $n=0$, the unique pairing on the zero space is an inner product.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space; the pairing is linear in its first argument ([[def-dimension]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). Write $\mathcal L(H)$ for its complex-linear endomorphisms ([[def-vector-space-of-linear-maps]]) and let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty outcome set. A **finite POVM** on $H$ with outcomes $\Omega$ is a family $E=(E_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ with each $E_a$ nonnegative and $\sum_{a\in\Omega}E_a=I_H$; after any enumeration of $\Omega$, these operators form the finite complete positive family of [[def-qc-finite-positive-effect-family]]. Reordering does not alter the finite sum. The complete-family lemma [[lem-qc-complete-effect-family-members-are-effects]] shows that every $E_a$ also has nonnegative complement $I_H-E_a$, so each is an effect.

For a density operator $\rho$ on $H$ (a nonnegative operator of trace one, [[def-qc-density-operator]]), its **POVM outcome weights** are

$$p_\rho(a):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_a),\qquad a\in\Omega.$$

Here $\operatorname{tr}$ is the finite-dimensional endomorphism trace ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]).

The positivity and normalization of these weights are proved in [[thm-qc-povm-probabilities-normalize]]. A POVM specifies this outcome law; it does not by itself prescribe a conditional output state.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space, let $K$ be a finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space, and let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty outcome set. A **finite instrument** from $H$ to $K$ is a family of complex-linear maps $\mathcal I_a:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$, one for each $a\in\Omega$, such that each $\mathcal I_a$ is completely positive ([[def-qc-completely-positive-map]]) and

$$\sum_{a\in\Omega}\operatorname{tr}_K(\mathcal I_a(X))=\operatorname{tr}_H(X)\qquad\text{for every }X\in\mathcal L(H).$$

For a density operator $\rho$ on $H$ (nonnegative with trace one, [[def-qc-density-operator]]), define the outcome weight $p_a(\rho):=\operatorname{tr}_K(\mathcal I_a(\rho))$. The **conditional state** for outcome $a$ is

$$\rho_a:=\begin{cases}\mathcal I_a(\rho)/p_a(\rho),&p_a(\rho)>0,\\[2pt]\bot,&p_a(\rho)=0.\end{cases}$$

Here $\bot$ is a symbol meaning that no conditional density operator is assigned; it is not a state. Positivity and normalization of the outcome weights, and density of every positive-probability conditional state, are proved in [[thm-qc-instrument-outcome-law-normalizes]] and [[thm-qc-instrument-conditional-state-is-density]].

In the ordered computational basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$ of [[def-qc-qubit-and-bloch-representation]], define the identity and Pauli endomorphisms of $Q_2$ by
$$I=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$

The displayed sign in $Y$ fixes all later orientation and rotation conventions.

in the ordered basis $|00\rangle,|01\rangle,|10\rangle,|11\rangle$. This is the exact controlled phase; no circuit cost or controlled access to an arbitrary black-box unitary is implied.

$$H:=\frac{X+Z}{\sqrt2}=\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad S:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&i\end{pmatrix},\qquad T:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&e^{i\pi/4}\end{pmatrix}.$$
The phases displayed in these matrices are exact; they are not identified modulo a scalar when the matrices are later placed under a control.

$$R_{\mathbf n}(\theta):=\exp\!\left(-\frac{i\theta}{2}\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}\right),\qquad R_z(\theta):=R_{(0,0,1)}(\theta).$$
Here $\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ and $\|\mathbf n\|_2$ have the meanings fixed in [[def-qc-bloch-coordinate-map]]. Its convergence applies here because $Q_2$ is finite-dimensional and complete and every linear endomorphism of $Q_2$ is bounded ([[cor-finite-dimensional-normed-spaces-are-banach]], [[cor-linear-maps-with-finite-dimensional-domain-are-bounded]]).

$$H:=\frac{X+Z}{\sqrt2}=\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad S:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&i\end{pmatrix},\qquad T:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&e^{i\pi/4}\end{pmatrix}.$$
The phases displayed in these matrices are exact; they are not identified modulo a scalar when the matrices are later placed under a control.

For real $\theta$ and a real unit vector $\mathbf n=(n_x,n_y,n_z)$, define the axis rotation
$$R_{\mathbf n}(\theta):=\exp\!\left(-\frac{i\theta}{2}\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}\right),\qquad R_z(\theta):=R_{(0,0,1)}(\theta).$$
Here $\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ and $\|\mathbf n\|_2$ have the meanings fixed in [[def-qc-bloch-coordinate-map]]. For a bounded endomorphism $B$ of $Q_2$, the notation $\exp(B)$ means the operator-norm series $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}B^k/k!$ of [[lem-exponential-series-of-a-bounded-operator]] at scalar parameter $1$. Its convergence applies here because $Q_2$ is finite-dimensional and complete and every linear endomorphism of $Q_2$ is bounded ([[cor-finite-dimensional-normed-spaces-are-banach]], [[cor-linear-maps-with-finite-dimensional-domain-are-bounded]]).

The unitary identities for the fixed matrices are verified below. The following theorem proves the closed form and unitarity of each $R_{\mathbf n}(\theta)$.

In the ordered computational basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$ of [[def-qc-qubit-and-bloch-representation]], define the identity and Pauli endomorphisms of $Q_2$ by
$$I=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$

The displayed sign in $Y$ fixes all later orientation and rotation conventions.

$$R_{\mathbf n}(\theta)=\exp\!\left(-\frac{i\theta}{2}\Sigma\right)=\cos(\theta/2)I-i\sin(\theta/2)\Sigma,$$
and $R_{\mathbf n}(\theta)$ is unitary. For the endpoint $\theta=0$, it equals $I$.

In the ordered two-qubit basis $|00\rangle,|01\rangle,|10\rangle,|11\rangle$, the controlled-NOT with first wire control and second wire target is

$$\operatorname{CNOT}_{1\to2}|a,t\rangle=|a,t\mathbin{\oplus}a\rangle,\qquad a,t\in\{0,1\}.$$

Equivalently, it is the control block $C(X)=\operatorname{diag}(I,X)$ of [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]], where $X$ is the Pauli bit-flip matrix. The wire order is part of the definition.

For a circuit with chronological layers $L_1,\ldots,L_d$, define

For $n\ge0$ and a binary word $x=(x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1})\in\{0,1\}^n$, define its
**big-endian index**

$$\operatorname{enc}_n(x):=\sum_{k<n}x_k\,2^{\,n-1-k}.$$

$\operatorname{enc}_0(())=0$. In an ordered $n$-qubit
computational basis, the word $x$ occupies the slot numbered
$\operatorname{enc}_n(x)$.

An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

Write $\mathcal Q_n$ for the ordered tensor product of $n$ copies of the two-level register from [[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]], with $\mathcal Q_0=\mathbb C$. derivations.claim: For $k>0$, put $m=2^k$ and, for $0\le j<m$, write $j$ as a $k$-bit word and set $p_j=j\oplus\lfloor j/2\rfloor$. In the arithmetic on these masks, bit $r=0$ is the least significant bit and controls are assigned to wires in reverse display order, as allowed by [F3]. In this proof, a control word $x$ is written in that same least-significant-first order, so it denotes the displayed register word $(x_{k-1},\ldots,x_0)$ and $\theta_x$ is the angle assigned to that displayed word; this is only a fixed reindexing of the finite branch set. The map is bijective: from $p_{k-1}=j_{k-1}$ and $p_r=j_{r+1}\oplus j_r$ one recovers the bits $j_r$ in descending order. Consecutive words $p_{j-1},p_j$ differ in exactly one coordinate: incrementing $j-1$ flips its trailing ones and the first zero, so in the Gray word all changed adjacent-bit XORs cancel except the bit at position $\nu_2(j)$, where $\nu_2(j)$ is the largest $r$ such that $2^r$ divides $j$. Also $p_0=0$ and $p_{m-1}=10\cdots0$, so the return from $p_{m-1}$ to $p_0$ changes one coordinate. Thus these words give a cyclic Gray traversal of all masks.

Set $$\beta_j:=2^{-k}\sum_{y\in\{0,1\}^k}(-1)^{p_j\cdot y}\theta_y.$$ For each fixed $x$, bijectivity of $j\mapsto p_j$ gives $$\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}(-1)^{p_j\cdot x}\beta_j =2^{-k}\sum_y\theta_y\sum_{p\in\{0,1\}^k}(-1)^{p\cdot(x\oplus y)} =\theta_x.$$ Indeed, the inner sum factors as $\prod_{r=0}^{k-1}(1+(-1)^{x_r\oplus y_r})$, equal to $2^k$ when $x=y$ and zero otherwise.

Write $\delta_j=p_{j-1}\oplus p_j$ for $1\le j<m$, and $\delta_m=p_{m-1}\oplus p_0$ for the return toggle. For a fixed control word $x$, the circuit matrix on the target is $$X^{\delta_m\cdot x}R_a(\beta_{m-1})X^{\delta_{m-1}\cdot x} R_a(\beta_{m-2})\cdots R_a(\beta_1)X^{\delta_1\cdot x}R_a(\beta_0).$$ The target-flip parity before rotation $j$ is $p_j\cdot x$. Direct multiplication of the matrices in [F1] gives, for both $a=y,z$, $XR_a(t)X=R_a(-t)$ and $R_a(s)R_a(t)=R_a(s+t)$. Moving each $X$ factor leftward through the preceding rotations gives angle sign $(-1)^{(\delta_{j+1}\oplus\cdots\oplus\delta_m)\cdot x} =(-1)^{p_j\cdot x}$ on $R_a(\beta_j)$, because the cyclic toggle sum is zero and $p_m=p_0=0$. No $X$ remains at the end. The rotations then combine to $R_a(\sum_j(-1)^{p_j\cdot x}\beta_j)=R_a(\theta_x)$ by step 2.1. The circuit consequently agrees with $M_a$ on every control basis subspace, and linearity gives equality on the whole register. It has $m$ rotations and $m$ CNOTs. For $k=0$ the sole term is $R_a(\theta_\emptyset)$ and needs no CNOT.

$$U=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\ C&D\end{pmatrix}.$$
There are block-diagonal unitaries $L=\operatorname{diag}(L_0,L_1)$ and $R=\operatorname{diag}(R_0,R_1)$ and nonnegative real diagonal matrices $C_0,S_0$ such that
$$U=L\begin{pmatrix}C_0&-S_0\\S_0&C_0\end{pmatrix}R,\qquad C_0^2+S_0^2=I,\quad 0\le C_0,S_0\le I.$$
The singular values at $0$ and $1$ are allowed, with no nondegeneracy assumption.

Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $U_0,U_1$ be unitary endomorphisms of $H$. On the control-first direct sum $H\oplus H$, the block unitary $\operatorname{diag}(U_0,U_1)$ factors as
$$\operatorname{diag}(U_0,U_1)=(I\otimes V)\operatorname{diag}(D,D^*)(I\otimes W)$$
for unitary $V,W$ on $H$ and a diagonal unitary $D$ in an orthonormal eigenbasis; $I\otimes V$ denotes $\operatorname{diag}(V,V)$ under $\mathbb C^2\otimes H\cong H\oplus H$.

For $k\ge0$ controls and real angles $\theta_x$ indexed by
$x\in\{0,1\}^k$, let
$$M_a=\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^k}|x\rangle\langle x|\otimes R_a(\theta_x), \qquad a\in\{y,z\},$$
where $R_y(\theta)=R_{(0,1,0)}(\theta)$ and
$R_z(\theta)=R_{(0,0,1)}(\theta)$ use the exact exponential convention of
[[def-qc-one-qubit-gate-alphabet-and-rotations]]. There is an exact finite
circuit for $M_a$ on the same $k+1$ wires, using arbitrary one-qubit
rotations and CNOT gates and no ancillas. For $k=0$ it is one rotation and no
CNOT; for $k>0$ it uses $2^k$ target rotations and $2^k$ CNOTs. The circuit
uses exact real angle labels; no finite-bit encoding or synthesis-time bound
is asserted.
Every $U\in U(4)$ has an exact circuit with no ancillas, at most three CNOT gates, and arbitrary one-qubit gates. The scalar phase is implemented as a one-qubit scalar gate and is not discarded.

Every $z\ne0$ has a unique representation $z=r(\cos\theta+i\sin\theta)$ with $r=|z|>0$ and $-\pi<\theta\le\pi$. The conventions and prerequisite facts used below are recorded in [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]], [[thm-sine-and-cosine-parametrize-the-unit-circle]], [[thm-sine-cosine-zero-sets-and-fundamental-period]].

Write $\mathcal Q_n$ for the ordered tensor product of $n$ copies of the two-level register from [[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]], with $\mathcal Q_0=\mathbb C$. For $n\ge0$, the circuit wire set is $[n]=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ in its displayed order and its state space is $\mathcal Q_n$. A gate occurrence on the $n$ wires is a pair $(g,(w_0,\ldots,w_{r(g)-1}))$ with distinct wire labels $w_j\in[n]$; the tuple order is the input and output factor order of the local gate. A layer is a finite ordered list of gate occurrences whose wire supports are pairwise disjoint. An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor

zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes

[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

Let $n\ge r\ge1$, let $w=(w_0,\ldots,w_{r-1})$ be an ordered tuple of distinct wires in $[n]$, and let $U:\mathcal Q_r\to\mathcal Q_r$ be unitary. Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph with a fixed vertex order. Let
$\mathcal H_V=\bigotimes_{v\in V}\mathbb C^2$ use that order and its ordered
computational basis, as in [[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]],
[[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]], and
[[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]. For each edge $\{u,v\}$ let
$CZ_{uv}$ be the unique full-register local embedding from
[[lem-qc-local-gate-wire-embedding]] of the controlled phase gate with angle
$\pi$ from [[def-qc-controlled-phase-rotation]]. Order the endpoints so that
$u$ precedes $v$ in the fixed vertex order; the embedded two-qubit matrix is
$\operatorname{diag}(1,1,1,-1)$ in the ordered pair basis
$|00\rangle,|01\rangle,|10\rangle,|11\rangle$, and every other tensor factor
acts as the identity. Thus the two local factors have the same order as the
edge endpoints, within the full register ordered by $V$. Order the finite edge
set lexicographically by its ordered endpoint indices and define

$$ |G\rangle:=\left(\prod_{\{u,v\}\in E}^{\mathrm{lex}}CZ_{uv}\right)|+\rangle^{\otimes V},\qquad |+\rangle=2^{-1/2}(|0\rangle+|1\rangle). $$

The lexicographic order makes the product a specified finite composition.
If $V=\varnothing$, the tensor product and empty product act on the
one-dimensional trivial register and $|G\rangle$ is its unit vector.

For any two edges $e,f$ of a finite simple graph on an ordered qubit register,
the embedded operators $CZ_e$ and $CZ_f$ commute. Consequently the finite
graph-state edge product is independent of the ordering of its edges.

For a real angle $\theta$, define the one-qubit phase matrix $P_\theta=\operatorname{diag}(1,e^{i\theta})$. In control-first order define

$$CP(\theta):=C(P_\theta)=\operatorname{diag}(1,1,1,e^{i\theta})$$

in the ordered basis $|00\rangle,|01\rangle,|10\rangle,|11\rangle$. This is the exact controlled phase; no circuit cost or controlled access to an arbitrary black-box unitary is implied.

Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph with a fixed order
$V=(v_0,\ldots,v_{n-1})$. Put $\mathbb F_2:=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$; the
field law follows from [[thm-z-mod-p-is-a-field]] at $p=2$, and this field has
order two by [[def-finite-field-and-its-order]]. Define the binary adjacency
matrix $A_2(G)\in M_n(\mathbb F_2)$ by

$$ (A_2(G))_{jk}=\begin{cases}1,&\{v_j,v_k\}\in E,\\0,&\{v_j,v_k\}\notin E.\end{cases} $$

The indices use the ordered bit coordinates of
[[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]]. Since edges are unordered pairs of
distinct vertices, $A_2(G)$ is symmetric and has zero diagonal. This is a
matrix over $\mathbb F_2$, using [[def-matrices-over-a-commutative-ring]];
it is not the root library's real-valued adjacency matrix. When $V=\varnothing$,
$A_2(G)$ is the unique $0\times0$ matrix.

In the ordered computational basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$ of [[def-qc-qubit-and-bloch-representation]], define the identity and Pauli endomorphisms of $Q_2$ by
$$I=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$

The displayed sign in $Y$ fixes all later orientation and rotation conventions.

The displayed tensor powers are tensor maps on the ordered factors, using [[def-qc-tensor-map]].
Fix an integer $n\ge 1$. Let $\mathcal H_n=Q_2^{\otimes n}$ be the ordered tensor register of $n$ qubits from [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], and let $\mathbb F_2=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$. We name the wires $1,\ldots,n$; wire $j$ is position $j-1$ in the source's $0$-based factor list. Bit tuples use the big-endian encoding from [[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]], so the first wire is the most significant bit. Write $X_j$ and $Z_j$ for the tensor maps with the displayed one-qubit matrix on wire $j$ and the identity on every other wire. For $x,z\in\mathbb F_2^n$, set $X^x=\bigotimes_{j=1}^n X^{x_j}$ and $Z^z=\bigotimes_{j=1}^n Z^{z_j}$, where an exponent $0$ means the identity on that factor and an exponent $1$ means the displayed Pauli matrix. For $k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z$, define

$$P(k,x,z):=i^kX^xZ^z.$$

The **phase-aware $n$-qubit Pauli set** $\mathcal P_n$ is the set of these operators with matrix multiplication. Its scalar subset is $Z_n:=\{i^k I_{\mathcal H_n}:k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z\}$. The product-and-adjoint theorem proves that $\mathcal P_n$ is a group and that $Z_n$ is its center.

For $a=(x,z)$ and $b=(x',z')$ in $V_n$ and any phases $k,k'$, 

$$P(k,x,z)P(k',x',z')=(-1)^{\omega(a,b)}P(k',x',z')P(k,x,z).$$

Thus the Pauli operators commute exactly when their labels are symplectically orthogonal.

derivations.claim: Every $CZ_{uv}$ is a diagonal Hermitian involution by [F2]. Conjugating $X_v$ by an incident gate gives $CZ_{uv}X_vCZ_{uv}=Z_uX_v$ by checking the four computational-basis pairs; a nonincident edge gate commutes with $X_v$. Since the edge gates commute by [F1], $U_GX_vU_G^\dagger=X_v\prod_{u\in N(v)}Z_u=K_v$. The tensor factors are Hermitian involutions, so $K_v$ is also a Hermitian involution.

The binary label of $K_v$ is $(e_v,A_2(G)e_v)$ because the $Z$ coordinate at $u$ is $(A_2(G)e_v)_u=(A_2(G))_{uv}$. For distinct $v,w$, the binary symplectic pairing of these labels is $e_v\cdot A_2(G)e_w+A_2(G)e_v\cdot e_w =(A_2(G))_{vw}+(A_2(G))_{wv}=0$ in $\mathbb F_2$ by [F3]. Thus [F5] gives pairwise commutation. Equivalently, when $\{v,w\}\in E$ the two local $X/Z$ anticommutations cancel, and when it is not an edge all overlapping factors are both $Z$ or act on different sites.
Using $X_v|+\rangle^{\otimes V}=|+\rangle^{\otimes V}$ and $U_G^\dagger=U_G$, we obtain $K_v|G\rangle=U_GX_vU_G^\dagger U_G|+\rangle^{\otimes V}=U_G|+\rangle^{\otimes V}=|G\rangle$.

In a product of generators indexed by $S\subseteq V$, the binary $X$-support is $\sum_{v\in S}e_v=1_S$ by [F4]. It vanishes only for $S=\varnothing$, so no nonempty product has identity binary label; the generators are independent. For empty $V$ this assertion is vacuous.

An **open-graph adaptive measurement pattern** consists of an ordered finite
simple graph $G=(V,E)$, input and output subsets $I,O\subseteq V$, an ordering
$m_1,\ldots,m_q$ of $M:=V\setminus O$, basis-choice functions
$\alpha_j:\{0,1\}^{j-1}\to\mathbb R$, and a terminal correction function
$C:\{0,1\}^q\to U(\mathcal H_O)$. For each subset $S\subseteq V$, write
$\mathcal H_S:=\bigotimes_{v\in S}\mathbb C^2$ in inherited vertex order,
with $\mathcal H_\varnothing=\mathbb C$. The tensor register $\mathcal H_V$
and all wire permutations use the fixed vertex order. Let
$\Pi_{I,V\setminus I}:\mathcal H_V\to
\mathcal H_I\otimes\mathcal H_{V\setminus I}$ be the wire permutation listing
$I$ first and then $V\setminus I$, each in inherited order. Let
$a_+:\mathbb C\to\mathbb C^2$ be the linear map $c\mapsto c|+\rangle$, and
let $a_{+,V\setminus I}:=\bigotimes_{v\in V\setminus I}a_+$ in inherited
order. Using the empty-tensor identifications, define the ordered input map
$$\iota_I:=\Pi_{I,V\setminus I}^{-1} (I_{\mathcal H_I}\otimes a_{+,V\setminus I}): \mathcal H_I\to\mathcal H_V.$$
Thus the input is unchanged and each complementary vertex receives $|+\rangle$.
Apply $U_G:=\prod_{\{u,v\}\in E}^{\mathrm{lex}}CZ_{uv}$.
At step $j$, after transcript prefix $b_1,\ldots,b_{j-1}$, measure vertex
$m_j$ in the ordered basis $\{|b_j\rangle_{\alpha_j(b_{<j})}:b_j\in\{0,1\}\}$
from [[def-qc-j-gate-and-equatorial-basis]]. The measured systems are removed
and the vertices in $O$ are retained in their inherited order.

Let $\Pi_{M,O}$ be the tensor permutation listing $m_1,\ldots,m_q$ first and
the vertices of $O$ in inherited order. For a full transcript
$\mathbf b=(b_1,\ldots,b_q)$, define the linear measurement contraction
$$B_{\mathbf b}:= \left(\bigotimes_{j=1}^q {}_{\alpha_j(b_{<j})}\!\langle b_j|_{m_j}\right)\otimes I_{\mathcal H_O},$$
where the bras are the linear functionals from
[[def-qc-dirac-notation-conversion]], their tensor map is formed in
$m_1,\ldots,m_q$ order, so
$B_{\mathbf b}:\mathcal H_{m_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathcal H_{m_q}
\otimes\mathcal H_O\to\mathcal H_O$. The scalar output
$\mathbb C^{\otimes q}$ is identified with
$\mathbb C$ by the tensor-unit convention. This tensor map is supplied by
[[def-qc-tensor-map]]; for $q=0$ its measured-register factor is the identity
on the empty tensor product. The branch map is the ordered composition

$$K_{\mathbf b}=B_{\mathbf b}\Pi_{M,O}U_G\iota_I: \mathcal H_I\to\mathcal H_O.$$

The measured systems are removed and the vertices in $O$ are retained in
their inherited order. This pattern uses $|V|$ qubit registers, its width in
the convention of [[def-qc-elementary-circuit-resources]]. Its projective
measurement count is $q$, counting one occurrence for each listed vertex
$m_j$. On a normalized pure input its
probability is $\|K_{\mathbf b}\psi\|^2$; for a density operator $\rho$ it is
$\operatorname{tr}(K_{\mathbf b}\rho K_{\mathbf b}^\dagger)$. The conditional
output is normalized only when that probability is positive. The corrected
branch is $C(\mathbf b)K_{\mathbf b}$; the correction does not change the
branch probability. This is a finite-dimensional mathematical circuit and
instrument semantics, with no physical postulate or implementation claim.

For $\alpha\in\mathbb R$, let
$P_\alpha=\operatorname{diag}(1,e^{i\alpha})$ and
$J(\alpha)=H P_\alpha$, with $H$ and the exact one-qubit gate convention
from [[def-qc-one-qubit-gate-alphabet-and-rotations]]. Define the ordered
measurement vectors

$$ |b\rangle_\alpha:=J(\alpha)^\dagger|b\rangle,\qquad b\in\{0,1\}, $$

where $|0\rangle,|1\rangle$ are the ordered computational basis vectors.
The adjoint and complex inner product use the root convention translated by
[[def-qc-dirac-notation-conversion]]. The global phase in $J(\alpha)$
is fixed by the displayed matrix product; it is not suppressed.

For every $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb R$, $J(\alpha)$ is unitary and
$\{|0\rangle_\alpha,|1\rangle_\alpha\}$ is an orthonormal basis. The exact
identities

$$ J(0)=H,\qquad J(0)^2=I,\qquad J(-\beta)X=e^{-i\beta}ZJ(\beta),\qquad J(\pi/2)^3=e^{i\pi/4}I $$

hold in the fixed phase convention.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty outcome set ([[def-dimension]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). Its **endomorphisms** are its complex-linear maps $H\to H$ ([[def-vector-space-of-linear-maps]]); for an endomorphism $P$, $P^*$ denotes its adjoint, which exists uniquely in finite dimension ([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]], [[thm-adjoint-exists-and-is-unique-in-finite-dimension]]). A **finite projective measurement** on $H$ with outcomes $\Omega$ is a family $(P_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ of endomorphisms such that

$$P_a^*=P_a,\qquad P_a^2=P_a,\qquad P_aP_b=0\ (a\ne b),\qquad \sum_{a\in\Omega}P_a=I_H.$$

The products above are compositions, the sum is pointwise addition of endomorphisms, and $I_H$ is the identity map; these operations preserve linear maps ([[prop-linear-maps-form-a-vector-space]], [[lem-composition-and-identity-linear-maps]]). The projections $P_a=0$ are permitted. For a density operator $\rho$ on $H$ (nonnegative and trace one, [[def-qc-density-operator]]), the associated outcome weights are $p_\rho(a)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_a)$; their nonnegativity and normalization are proved in [[thm-qc-projective-measurement-outcome-law]].

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root library's convention that the inner product is linear in its first argument. A **density operator** on $H$ is a non-negative endomorphism $\rho:H\to H$ with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho)=1$; non-negative and trace have the meanings of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]] and [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. The zero-dimensional space is excluded: its only endomorphism has trace $0$.

Here $\ker\rho=\{x\in H:\rho x=0\}$, using the kernel of a linear map from [[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]. The **support** of $\rho$ is the orthogonal complement of its kernel in the root convention:

$$\operatorname{supp}(\rho):=\{x\in H: \langle x,y\rangle=0\text{ for every }y\in\ker\rho\}.$$

For a subspace $S\subseteq H$, $\rho$ is **faithful on $S$** when $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)=S$ and the restriction $\rho|_S:S\to S$ is positive definite in the sense of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]. This restriction is an endomorphism: if $x\in S$ and $y\in\ker\rho$, self-adjointness gives $\langle\rho x,y\rangle=\langle x,\rho y\rangle=0$, so $\rho x\in(\ker\rho)^\perp=S$.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $F$ and let $T:V\to V$ be
linear. Choose any ordered basis $\mathcal B$ of $V$ and define the **trace of
the endomorphism $T$** by

$$\operatorname{tr}(T):=\operatorname{tr}([T]_{\mathcal B}^{\mathcal B}).$$

This is independent of the chosen basis: matrices of the same endomorphism in
two ordered bases are similar, and similar matrices have equal trace. When
$V$ is the zero space, the empty basis gives trace $0$.

For $A\in M_{m\times n}(F)$ and $B\in M_{n\times m}(F)$,

$$\operatorname{tr}(AB)=\operatorname{tr}(BA).$$

The two products may have different sizes, and the equality includes $m=0$ or
$n=0$.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real or complex inner product space and let
$T:V\to V$ be linear. The operator $T$ is **non-negative** when $T$ is
self-adjoint in the sense of [[def-self-adjoint-and-normal-endomorphism]] and

$$\langle Tv,v\rangle\ge 0$$

for every $v\in V$.

The operator $T$ is **positive** when $T$ is self-adjoint and

$$\langle Tv,v\rangle>0$$

for every nonzero $v\in V$.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real or complex inner product space and let
$T:V\to V$ be linear. The following are equivalent:

1. $T$ is non-negative.
2. $T$ is self-adjoint and every eigenvalue of $T$ is a nonnegative real number.
3. Some orthonormal basis makes the matrix of $T$ diagonal with nonnegative real diagonal entries.
4. There exists a linear map $S:V\to V$ such that $T=S^*S$.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space. Two nonzero vectors $x,y\in H$ represent the same **ray** when $y=\alpha x$ for some nonzero $\alpha\in\mathbb C$. A **pure state** is such a ray. If $u$ is a unit representative, its associated operator is $P_u=|u\rangle\langle u|$, with the bra, ket and outer-product convention of [[def-qc-dirac-notation-conversion]]. The theorem [[thm-qc-ray-projector-well-defined-and-bijective]] proves that this operator is a rank-one orthogonal projection independent of the chosen unit representative, so it is the operator representative of the pure state.

All complex inner products in this track use the root convention: they are
linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second
([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). For vectors $x,y$ in the same
space, define the Dirac pairing by

$$\langle x|y\rangle_D:=\langle y,x\rangle_{\mathrm{root}}.$$

The ket $|x\rangle$ denotes the vector $x$. The bra $\langle x|$ denotes the
linear functional $z\mapsto\langle z,x\rangle_{\mathrm{root}}$.

For finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H,K$, vectors $y\in H$ and
$x\in K$, define the rank-one linear map

$$|x\rangle\langle y|:H\to K,\qquad z\mapsto\langle z,y\rangle_{H,\mathrm{root}}x.$$

Given ordered orthonormal bases of $H$ and $K$, its coordinate matrix is
$[x][y]^\dagger$, where $[x]$ and $[y]$ are the corresponding coordinate
columns and $M^\dagger:=\overline M^{\mathsf T}$ is the conjugate transpose.
The coordinate assertion is established in
[[thm-qc-dirac-notation-coordinate-identity]].

Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces with ordered
orthonormal bases $E=(e_j)_{j<n}$ and $F=(f_i)_{i<m}$. Let $T:H\to K$ be
linear ([[def-linear-map]]), and write $T_{ij}$ for the $(i,j)$ entry of its
matrix in these bases.
Then, for every $z\in H$,

$$Tz=\sum_{j<n}\sum_{i<m}T_{ij}\langle z,e_j\rangle_{H,\mathrm{root}}f_i, \qquad T=\sum_{j<n}\sum_{i<m}T_{ij}|f_i\rangle\langle e_j|.$$

For $x\in K$ and $y\in H$, the rank-one map $|x\rangle\langle y|$ has
coordinate matrix $[x]_F[y]_E^\dagger$, where $M^\dagger=\overline M^{\mathsf T}$.
Its amplitude satisfies
$\langle x|T|y\rangle_D=\langle Ty,x\rangle_{K,\mathrm{root}}$.
All sums are empty when an index dimension is zero, and the identities include
those cases.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space, let $K$ be a finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space, and let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty outcome set. A **finite instrument** from $H$ to $K$ is a family of complex-linear maps $\mathcal I_a:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$, one for each $a\in\Omega$, such that each $\mathcal I_a$ is completely positive ([[def-qc-completely-positive-map]]) and

$$\sum_{a\in\Omega}\operatorname{tr}_K(\mathcal I_a(X))=\operatorname{tr}_H(X)\qquad\text{for every }X\in\mathcal L(H).$$

For a density operator $\rho$ on $H$ (nonnegative with trace one, [[def-qc-density-operator]]), define the outcome weight $p_a(\rho):=\operatorname{tr}_K(\mathcal I_a(\rho))$. The **conditional state** for outcome $a$ is

$$\rho_a:=\begin{cases}\mathcal I_a(\rho)/p_a(\rho),&p_a(\rho)>0,\\[2pt]\bot,&p_a(\rho)=0.\end{cases}$$

Here $\bot$ is a symbol meaning that no conditional density operator is assigned; it is not a state. Positivity and normalization of the outcome weights, and density of every positive-probability conditional state, are proved in [[thm-qc-instrument-outcome-law-normalizes]] and [[thm-qc-instrument-conditional-state-is-density]].

For a real angle $\theta$, define the one-qubit phase matrix $P_\theta=\operatorname{diag}(1,e^{i\theta})$. In control-first order define

$$CP(\theta):=C(P_\theta)=\operatorname{diag}(1,1,1,e^{i\theta})$$

in the ordered basis $|00\rangle,|01\rangle,|10\rangle,|11\rangle$. This is the exact controlled phase; no circuit cost or controlled access to an arbitrary black-box unitary is implied.

For an integer $d\ge 1$, the $d$-level register is the complex inner-product
space $Q_d=\mathbb C^d$ with the standard pairing
$\langle z,w\rangle_{\rm root}=\sum_{j<d}z_j\overline{w_j}$, linear in the
first argument as in [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]] and
[[prop-standard-coordinate-inner-products]]. Its **computational basis** is the
ordered standard basis $(e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1})$ of [[lem-standard-basis-of-f-n]].
The register's alphabet is the ordered set $\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$.

For $n\ge0$, the $n$-qubit register is the ordered tensor product over
$\mathbb C$ of $n$ copies of $Q_2$. Here $\otimes_{\mathbb C}$ is the algebraic
module tensor product ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]),
with its complex-module structure and finite iterated/empty-product conventions
from [[thm-commutative-ring-module-structure-on-a-tensor-product]] and
[[cor-finite-iterated-tensor-products-represent-multilinear-maps]]. The tuple of
bit positions is ordered lexicographically, with the first wire as the most
significant position; the product-basis theorem below establishes the
corresponding elementary tensors as a basis. For $n=0$, the empty tensor
product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. This one-dimensional trivial
register is distinct from the zero vector space $\mathbb C^0$. By definition a
register has positive dimension; a zero-dimensional space may still occur as a
factor in the more general tensor-space construction below.

For every $d\ge1$, the ordered computational basis $(e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1})$ of
the register $Q_d$ from [[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]] is an
orthonormal basis for its declared inner product. Separately, the one-dimensional
zero-qubit register has the basis $\{1\}$ by definition.

An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

derivations.claim: For $0\le j\le q$, put $R_j:=V\setminus\{m_1,\ldots,m_j\}$ and let $\Pi_j:\mathcal H_V\to\mathcal H_{m_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes \mathcal H_{m_j}\otimes\mathcal H_{R_j}$ be the wire permutation listing the first $j$ measured vertices in measurement order and the remainder in inherited order. For a prefix $\mathbf c=(c_1,\ldots,c_j)$, let $B_{\mathbf c}:=\bigotimes_{t=1}^j{}_{\alpha_t(c_{<t})}\!\langle c_t|_{m_t}$ be the tensor map of its linear measurement bras, with its scalar output $\mathbb C^{\otimes j}$ identified with $\mathbb C$, and define $K_{\mathbf c}:=(B_{\mathbf c}\otimes I_{R_j})\Pi_jU_G\iota_I: \mathcal H_I\to\mathcal H_{R_j}$. For $j=0$, the empty tensor map and permutation are identities, so $K_\emptyset=U_G\iota_I$. If $j<q$, let $Q_{j+1}:\mathcal H_{R_j}\to\mathcal H_{m_{j+1}}\otimes\mathcal H_{R_{j+1}}$ list the next measured vertex first, and put $L_{b|\mathbf c}:=({}_{\alpha_{j+1}(\mathbf c)}\!\langle b|_{m_{j+1}} \otimes I_{R_{j+1}})Q_{j+1}$. Under canonical associations, $B_{\mathbf c b}=B_{\mathbf c}\otimes {}_{\alpha_{j+1}(\mathbf c)}\!\langle b|_{m_{j+1}}$ and $\Pi_{j+1}=(I_{\mathcal H_{m_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathcal H_{m_j}} \otimes Q_{j+1})\Pi_j$. Tensor-map factorwise action and permutation composition therefore give $K_{\mathbf c b}=L_{b|\mathbf c}K_{\mathbf c}$. At $j=q$, $R_q=O$, $\Pi_q=\Pi_{M,O}$, and this recursive map is exactly the full branch map in the Definition. Set $\sigma_{\mathbf c}:=K_{\mathbf c}\rho K_{\mathbf c}^\dagger$. At the root it is nonnegative since it is a congruence of $\rho$ by $U_G\iota_I$. At every prefix, nonnegativity of $\sigma_{\mathbf c}$ gives $\langle L_{b|\mathbf c}\sigma_{\mathbf c}L_{b|\mathbf c}^\dagger v,v\rangle =\langle\sigma_{\mathbf c}L_{b|\mathbf c}^\dagger v, L_{b|\mathbf c}^\dagger v\rangle\ge0$, so each child state is nonnegative. Orthonormality in [F2] gives $\sum_{b=0}^1L_{b|\mathbf c}^\dagger L_{b|\mathbf c}=I_{R_j}$. By trace cyclicity [F4], the two child traces sum to $\operatorname{tr}(\sigma_{\mathbf c})$.

The root state is $U_G\iota_I\rho\iota_I^\dagger U_G^\dagger$, where $\iota_I$ tensors the unit $|+\rangle$ ancillas and $U_G$ is the finite edge-gate product in [F1]. By [F8], $\iota_I^\dagger\iota_I=I$ and $U_G^\dagger U_G=I$; trace cyclicity [F4] therefore gives root trace $\operatorname{tr}(\rho)=1$. Repeatedly applying the trace identity of step 1.1 down the finite binary tree preserves the sum of leaf traces. By the terminal identity in step 1.1, the leaf state is the stated $K_{\mathbf b}\rho K_{\mathbf b}^\dagger$, so $\sum_{\mathbf b}\operatorname{tr}(K_{\mathbf b}\rho K_{\mathbf b}^\dagger)=1$. When there are no measurements, the unique empty transcript has the same trace as this root state.

For a pure input $\rho=|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|$, the branch output is $|K_{\mathbf b}\psi\rangle\langle K_{\mathbf b}\psi|$ by [F6], so its trace is $\|K_{\mathbf b}|\psi\rangle\|^2$ by the coordinate formula in [F6]. For a density input the branch probability is the branch-output trace in step 2.1.

Each branch output $K_{\mathbf b}\rho K_{\mathbf b}^\dagger$ is nonnegative because $\langle K_{\mathbf b}\rho K_{\mathbf b}^\dagger v,v\rangle=\langle\rho K_{\mathbf b}^\dagger v,K_{\mathbf b}^\dagger v\rangle\ge0$ by [F3]. Its trace is therefore nonnegative by [F5]. If that trace is zero, the nonnegative eigenvalues in [F5] sum to zero by [F4], so each is zero and the output operator is zero. For a pure input, step 3.1 then gives $K_{\mathbf b}|\psi\rangle=0$. In either case [F7] leaves no normalized conditional state; for positive probability the indicated division is defined.

The finite edge-gate list denotes its chronological product by [F3], and the ordered measurement contractions compose after that product. The resulting branch maps are exactly the $K_{\mathbf b}$ of [F1], with input register $\mathcal H_I$, output register $\mathcal H_O$, and finite outcome set $\{0,1\}^q$. This finite specification has one wire per vertex, one $CZ$ occurrence per edge, and one measurement occurrence per listed measured vertex, so [F5] gives the stated resource coordinates. The set of exact angle and correction labels is finite because both the vertex set and transcript set are finite; no finite-bit encoding or synthesis-time claim follows.

For each transcript define $\mathcal I_{\mathbf b}(X):= K_{\mathbf b}XK_{\mathbf b}^*$. Each branch map is completely positive: for any finite reference register and positive $Y$, its extension sends $Y$ to $(I\otimes K_{\mathbf b})Y(I\otimes K_{\mathbf b}^*)$, which is positive. Let $A:=\sum_{\mathbf b}K_{\mathbf b}^*K_{\mathbf b}$. For every unit vector $u$, [F6] applied to $|u\rangle\langle u|$ gives $\langle Au,u\rangle=\sum_{\mathbf b}\|K_{\mathbf b}u\|^2=1$. In an orthonormal basis, applying this identity to each basis vector shows the diagonal entries of $A-I$ vanish; applying it to $(e_j+e_k)/\sqrt2$ and $(e_j+i e_k)/\sqrt2$ shows the real and imaginary parts of each off-diagonal entry vanish. Hence $A=I$. By trace cyclicity [F8], $\sum_{\mathbf b}\operatorname{tr}(\mathcal I_{\mathbf b}(X)) =\operatorname{tr}(XA)=\operatorname{tr}(X)$ for every operator $X$. Thus these maps form a finite instrument from $\mathcal H_I$ to $\mathcal H_O$ by [F7].

For density input $\rho$, step 1.1 gives exactly the same raw branch state $K_{\mathbf b}\rho K_{\mathbf b}^*$ in the raw circuit and raw pattern. Its trace is $p_{\mathbf b}$, and division by that trace gives the same $\rho_{\mathbf b}$ when $p_{\mathbf b}>0$. The controller in [F4] stores the observed transcript and appends $C(\mathbf b)$, giving the exact corrected branch operator $L_{\mathbf b}=C(\mathbf b)K_{\mathbf b}$ in both corrected presentations. Unitarity gives $L_{\mathbf b}^*L_{\mathbf b}=K_{\mathbf b}^*K_{\mathbf b}$, so cyclicity [F8] gives the same probability. Normalizing gives $C(\mathbf b)\rho_{\mathbf b}C(\mathbf b)^*$ on positive branches. There is no normalized output on zero-probability branches.

Retaining the transcript associates each $\mathbf b$ to the raw map $X\mapsto K_{\mathbf b}XK_{\mathbf b}^*$ or to the corrected map $X\mapsto L_{\mathbf b}XL_{\mathbf b}^*$, respectively. Corresponding maps agree exactly in the two raw or two corrected presentations. The corrected maps are completely positive by the same reference-register calculation as in step 1.2, and $\sum_{\mathbf b}L_{\mathbf b}^*L_{\mathbf b}=I$ by step 1.2 and step 2.1, so they too form an instrument. supports by [[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]], so no $J$ gate in

[[lem-qc-disjoint-layer-order-independence]], its denotation may be written
with the CZ matching first and then at most one $J(\alpha_{rj})$ per schedule
index $j$. The

list of rounds $(M_s,(\alpha_{s1},\ldots,\alpha_{sn}))$ and the scalar

one $J$ gate on each wire. Define

matching case below; the empty product is $1$. This order makes the
zero-wire empty-layer case unambiguous:

2. If $n\ge1$ and $J_r=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, the block consists of one round with matching

indices without an original $J$ gate are padding angles. For a mixed layer,

graph's simplicity is part of this definition.

At step $j$, after transcript prefix $b_1,\ldots,b_{j-1}$, measure vertex
$m_j$ in the ordered basis $\{|b_j\rangle_{\alpha_j(b_{<j})}:b_j\in\{0,1\}\}$
from [[def-qc-j-gate-and-equatorial-basis]]. The measured systems are removed
and the vertices in $O$ are retained in their inherited order.

Let $\Pi_{M,O}$ be the tensor permutation listing $m_1,\ldots,m_q$ first and
the vertices of $O$ in inherited order. For a full transcript
$\mathbf b=(b_1,\ldots,b_q)$, define the linear measurement contraction
$$B_{\mathbf b}:= \left(\bigotimes_{j=1}^q {}_{\alpha_j(b_{<j})}\!\langle b_j|_{m_j}\right)\otimes I_{\mathcal H_O},$$
where the bras are the linear functionals from
[[def-qc-dirac-notation-conversion]], their tensor map is formed in
$m_1,\ldots,m_q$ order, so
$B_{\mathbf b}:\mathcal H_{m_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathcal H_{m_q}
\otimes\mathcal H_O\to\mathcal H_O$. The scalar output
$\mathbb C^{\otimes q}$ is identified with
$\mathbb C$ by the tensor-unit convention. This tensor map is supplied by
[[def-qc-tensor-map]]; for $q=0$ its measured-register factor is the identity
on the empty tensor product. The branch map is the ordered composition

$$K_{\mathbf b}=B_{\mathbf b}\Pi_{M,O}U_G\iota_I: \mathcal H_I\to\mathcal H_O.$$

The measured systems are removed and the vertices in $O$ are retained in
their inherited order. This pattern uses $|V|$ qubit registers, its width in
the convention of [[def-qc-elementary-circuit-resources]]. Its projective
measurement count is $q$, counting one occurrence for each listed vertex
$m_j$. On a normalized pure input its
probability is $\|K_{\mathbf b}\psi\|^2$; for a density operator $\rho$ it is
$\operatorname{tr}(K_{\mathbf b}\rho K_{\mathbf b}^\dagger)$. The conditional
output is normalized only when that probability is positive. The corrected
branch is $C(\mathbf b)K_{\mathbf b}$; the correction does not change the
branch probability. This is a finite-dimensional mathematical circuit and
instrument semantics, with no physical postulate or implementation claim.

Let $C$ be a finite J/CZ circuit and let $\mathcal T(C)$ have rounds
$(M_s,(\alpha_{s1},\ldots,\alpha_{sn}))_{s=1}^R$ and recorded scalar
$\sigma_C$ as in [[def-qc-normalized-transport-schedule]]. The schedule index
$j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$ denotes source circuit wire $j-1$; thus a schedule edge
$\{j,k\}$ corresponds to the source-wire pair $\{j-1,k-1\}$. Coordinate
$j$ of every frame vector denotes this same wire. The encoded graph
$G_C$ has vertices $v_{j,s}$ for $1\le j\le n$ and $0\le s\le R$,
horizontal edges $\{v_{j,s-1},v_{j,s}\}$, and vertical edges
$\{v_{j,s-1},v_{k,s-1}\}$ for $\{j,k\}\in M_s$. It is a finite simple
graph by [[lem-qc-transport-encoding-is-simple-and-size-bounded]]. Its input
vertices are $I=\{v_{j,0}:1\le j\le n\}$, its outputs are
$O=\{v_{j,R}:1\le j\le n\}$, and its ordered vertex register follows wire
index first and then column index. In particular, the inherited orders on
$I$ and $O$ are $v_{1,0},\ldots,v_{n,0}$ and
$v_{1,R},\ldots,v_{n,R}$, matching source circuit wire order
$0,\ldots,n-1$. The pattern’s measurement order on the vertices
$v_{j,s-1}$ is round-major, wire-minor, for $s=1,\ldots,R$ and
$j=1,\ldots,n$.

The adaptive basis angles and terminal correction are defined from the
outcome blocks $b^s=(b^s_1,\ldots,b^s_n)$ as follows. Let $A_s$ be the binary
adjacency matrix of $M_s$ with vertex order $1,\ldots,n$ (vertex $j$ is
position $j-1$ in the zero-based order of [[def-qc-binary-adjacency-matrix]]),
so
$(A_s)_{jk}=1$ exactly when $\{j,k\}\in M_s$. Matrix-vector products and
all frame vectors use these coordinates; binary dot products mean
$u\cdot v=\sum_{j=1}^n u_jv_j\in\mathbb F_2$. The frame functions are defined recursively by
$x^0=z^0=0\in\mathbb F_2^n$ and the following formulas. Before round $s$, define

$$z^{s,*}:=z^{s-1}\oplus A_sx^{s-1},\qquad \theta_{sj}:=(-1)^{x^{s-1}_j}\alpha_{sj}.$$

For an outcome block $b^s$, the post-round frame is defined by
$x^s:=b^s\oplus z^{s,*}$ and $z^s:=x^{s-1}$. The function of earlier
outcomes given by these recurrences selects the equatorial measurement basis
at each vertex. For a complete transcript $\mathbf b$, the
terminal frame and correction are the following functions. For $n\ge1$, the zero-scalar Pauli frame is
$P(x,z):=X^xZ^z=P(0,x,z)$ from
[[def-qc-phase-aware-n-qubit-pauli-group]], and the terminal correction is
$C(\mathbf b):=P(x^R,z^R)^\dagger$. For $n=0$, the empty frame is
$P((),()):=I_{\mathbb C}$ and the correction is the identity on the
one-dimensional register.

For $n\ge1$, define
$\gamma(x,z,\alpha)=1$ if $x=0$ and
$\gamma(x,z,\alpha)=(-1)^ze^{-i\alpha}$ if $x=1$, as in
[[lem-qc-adaptive-angle-pauli-frame-update]], and put

$$\lambda_{\mathbf b}:=\sigma_C\prod_{s=1}^R\left[ (-1)^{\sum_{\{j,k\}\in M_s}x^{s-1}_jx^{s-1}_k} \prod_{j=1}^n\gamma(x^{s-1}_j,z^{s,*}_j,\alpha_{sj})\right].$$

For $n=0$, the empty transcript has scalar $\lambda=1$. The encoding
retains these exact scalars; no global phase is discarded. Its graph has
$n(R+1)$ vertices and $R\le3d$ for $d$ original layers. The item
[[lem-qc-normalized-rounds-preserve-circuit]] proves that the normalized
round circuit is $\sigma_C U_C$; the branch theorem proves the resulting
pattern's relation to $U_C$.

For a normalized qubit $|\psi\rangle=a|0\rangle+c|1\rangle$ and real
$\alpha$, prepare $CZ(|\psi\rangle\otimes|+\rangle)$ and project the first
qubit in the ordered basis $\{|b\rangle_\alpha:b=0,1\}$ of
[[def-qc-j-gate-and-equatorial-basis]]. The outcome-$b$ branch operator on the
second qubit is

$$K_b=2^{-1/2}X^bJ(\alpha).$$

Thus each outcome has probability $1/2$ and the normalized output is
$X^bJ(\alpha)|\psi\rangle$. The operator identity is linear and therefore
also holds when the input qubit is entangled with a finite-dimensional
reference register.

Let a one-qubit input carry the Pauli frame $X^xZ^z$, where $x,z\in\{0,1\}$,
and let $\beta\in\mathbb R$. Choose the next equatorial measurement angle
$(-1)^x\beta$. For outcome $b\in\{0,1\}$, the one-bit teleportation branch is

$$ 2^{-1/2}\gamma(x,z,\beta)X^{b\oplus z}Z^xJ(\beta),\qquad \gamma(x,z,\beta)=\begin{cases}1,&x=0,\\(-1)^ze^{-i\beta},&x=1.\end{cases} $$

Thus the updated Pauli frame is $(x',z')=(b\oplus z,x)$, and the exact
branch scalar has unit modulus.

Let $n\ge0$ and let $M$ be a matching, meaning a set of pairwise disjoint
two-element subsets of the ordered wire set $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Give the graph
$G_M=(\{1,\ldots,n\},M)$ the vertex order $1,\ldots,n$, so vertex $j$ is
coordinate $j$ (position $j-1$ in the zero-based vertex list) of its binary
adjacency matrix. Let $A_M:=A_2(G_M)\in M_n(\mathbb F_2)$ from
[[def-qc-binary-adjacency-matrix]], so $(A_M)_{jk}=1$ exactly when
$\{j,k\}\in M$. For $x,z\in\mathbb F_2^n$, all coordinates use this wire
order, and binary dot products mean $a\cdot b:=\sum_{j=1}^n a_jb_j$ in
$\mathbb F_2$. Define $q_M(x):=\sum_{\{j,k\}\in M}x_jx_k\in\mathbb F_2$.
For $n\ge1$, put
$P(x,z):=X^xZ^z=P(0,x,z)$ as in
[[def-qc-phase-aware-n-qubit-pauli-group]]. For $n=0$, the unique empty
vectors satisfy $X^x=Z^z=I_{\mathbb C}$ and we define $P(x,z)=I_{\mathbb C}$;
the register is the empty tensor product from
[[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]. With
$CZ_M:=\prod_{\{j,k\}\in M}CZ_{jk}$,

$$CZ_M P(x,z)=(-1)^{q_M(x)}P(x,z\oplus A_Mx)CZ_M.$$

For the empty wire set or empty matching the sum is zero and the formula is
the identity.

For any two edges $e,f$ of a finite simple graph on an ordered qubit register,
the embedded operators $CZ_e$ and $CZ_f$ commute. Consequently the finite
graph-state edge product is independent of the ordering of its edges.

For a finite adaptive pattern with transcript branch maps $K_{\mathbf b}$, a
normalized pure input $|\psi\rangle$ has
$p_{\mathbf b}=\|K_{\mathbf b}|\psi\rangle\|^2$ and
$\sum_{\mathbf b}p_{\mathbf b}=1$. For a density operator $\rho$, the branch
probability is $p_{\mathbf b}=\operatorname{tr}(K_{\mathbf b}\rho
K_{\mathbf b}^\dagger)$ and these probabilities also sum to one. A transcript
with $p_{\mathbf b}=0$ is impossible and has no normalized conditional output;
normalization is defined only for positive-probability branches.

If square matrices $A$ and $B$ over $F$ are similar, then
$\operatorname{tr}(A)=\operatorname{tr}(B)$.

For a gate occurrence $g=(\gamma,w)$ in a circuit on $\mathcal Q_n$, let $\widetilde U_g$ be the global embedding from [[lem-qc-local-gate-wire-embedding]]. For a layer $L_t=(g_1,\ldots,g_s)$, define
$$U_{L_t}:=\widetilde U_{g_s}\cdots\widetilde U_{g_1}.$$
For a circuit with chronological layers $L_1,\ldots,L_d$, define
$$U_C:=U_{L_d}\cdots U_{L_1}.$$
The empty circuit and every empty layer denote the identity on $\mathcal Q_n$.

An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

derivations.claim: By [F8], the graph state's finite product of edge gates may be reordered without changing it. For round $s$, the vertical edges from $M_s$ act on column $s-1$ before that column is measured, and the horizontal edges from column $s-1$ to $s$ form one one-bit transport on each wire. The tensor factors of these $n$ transports are disjoint; later vertical edges act on later columns and do not change an earlier measurement projector. The ordered pattern in [F4] therefore realizes the round-wise sequence of matching and horizontal transports.

Suppose the logical state entering round $s$ is represented with frame $P(x^{s-1},z^{s-1})$. The matching relation [F7] moves that frame past $CZ_{M_s}$, contributes $\mu_s=(-1)^{q_{M_s}(x^{s-1})}$, and changes its $Z$ vector to $z^{s,*}=z^{s-1}\oplus A_sx^{s-1}$. Applying [F6] on wire $j$ with angle $\alpha_{sj}$ and outcome $b_j^s$ gives the new frame bits $x_j^s=b_j^s\oplus z_j^{s,*}$ and $z_j^s=x_j^{s-1}$ and contributes $2^{-1/2}\gamma(x_j^{s-1},z_j^{s,*},\alpha_{sj})$. Tensoring the $n$ one-wire identities gives round factor $2^{-n/2}\mu_s\prod_j\gamma(x_j^{s-1},z_j^{s,*},\alpha_{sj})$ and applies the round unitary after the prior logical unitary.

Initially $x^0=z^0=0$ and the branch map is the identity. Induction on $s$ using step 1.2 gives, for the first $s$ outcome blocks, the scalar $2^{-ns/2}$, the recursively specified Pauli frame, and the chronological product of the first $s$ normalized round unitaries. At $s=R$, [F2] turns that logical product into $\sigma_CU_C$, so the accumulated scalar equals the explicit $\lambda_{\mathbf b}$ of the encoding. Therefore $K_{\mathbf b}=2^{-nR/2}\lambda_{\mathbf b}P_{\mathbf b}U_C$.

Both $P_{\mathbf b}$ and $U_C$ are unitary and $|\lambda_{\mathbf b}|=1$. Thus a normalized pure input has branch probability $2^{-nR}$ by [F9]. For a density operator $\rho$, the branch output is $2^{-nR}P_{\mathbf b}U_C\rho U_C^{\dagger}P_{\mathbf b}^{\dagger}$; unitary conjugation is a similarity, so [F10] gives its trace as $2^{-nR}\operatorname{tr}(\rho)=2^{-nR}$. The transcript has $nR$ binary outcomes, hence $2^{nR}$ leaves and total probability one.

Applying $P_{\mathbf b}^{\dagger}$ to each branch leaves $2^{-nR/2}\lambda_{\mathbf b}U_C$. On pure inputs this differs from $U_C|\psi\rangle$ only by a nonzero scalar, so it has the same output ray. On density inputs, summing the corrected branch maps gives $2^{-nR}\sum_{\mathbf b}U_C\rho U_C^{\dagger}=U_C\rho U_C^{\dagger}$, because there are $2^{nR}$ transcripts. If $R=0$, there is one empty transcript and the schedule contains only empty layers; if $n=0$, there is one empty transcript on the one-dimensional register. The formula gives the identity in both boundary cases.
